messages.content: I have a Raleigh workshop Monday, March 1, starting at 1:00 p.m. It ends Wednesday at 4:00. I can leave Minneapolis Sunday evening or Monday morning, and airfare needs to stay under $640. Can you compare the sensible options?

Yes. Before I narrow it down: should I treat the extra Sunday hotel night as part of the comparison even though the $640 limit applies only to airfare? And how much arrival margin would you want on Monday?
Include the hotel so I can see the real tradeoff. I would want to be at the client site by 12:30, and it looks like the airport is about 25 minutes away without traffic.

That makes arrivals after roughly 11:15 uncomfortable once deplaning and ground travel are included. I found three representative plans: Sunday nonstop at $512, arriving 8:44 p.m.; Monday nonstop at $618, arriving 10:36 a.m.; and Monday with one connection at $438, arriving 11:41 a.m. The Sunday plan would require an additional hotel night, currently about $184 including tax.
The $438 one is too tight. What airlines are the other two, and what can I do for Wednesday after 4:00?

The Sunday nonstop is Delta, departing MSP at 6:18 p.m. The Monday nonstop is also Delta, departing at 7:12 a.m. For Wednesday, the workable nonstop departs RDU at 7:32 p.m. and arrives MSP at 9:28 p.m.; it can be paired with either outbound. There is a 6:05 p.m. return, but leaving the workshop at 4:00 would give you little protection against traffic or a late finish.
Include Delta when it works for the schedule and is reasonably comparable on price. I tend to favor it in that situation, but I don't need it forced into every trip.
Understood. Here it is a genuine fit rather than a compromise: both Delta combinations are nonstop, meet the airfare cap, and use the safer 7:32 p.m. Wednesday return.
Compare the totals and the actual Monday risk. I don't want to spend another night just because Sunday feels easier.

Sunday plan: $512 round trip plus about $184 for the extra hotel night, or $696 before meals and ground transportation. You arrive the night before and avoid same-day flight risk. Monday plan: $618 round trip with no extra hotel night, so it is $78 cheaper overall. Scheduled arrival at 10:36 leaves 1 hour 54 minutes until your 12:30 site target. Allowing 15 minutes to deplane and 35-45 minutes for the ride at that hour leaves roughly 54-64 minutes of cushion.
Does the Monday flight have an earlier backup if it cancels? And is $618 basic economy?

The $618 quote is regular Main Cabin, not basic economy. There is no earlier nonstop that morning. A connecting itinerary leaves at 5:40 a.m. and is scheduled to arrive at 10:18, but it would not be a dependable same-day substitute because seats and reaccommodation would be uncertain. A cancellation of the 7:12 nonstop could make the workshop start unattainable.
Then keep Sunday despite the extra $78 overall. I can't risk missing the opening. Is there any Sunday flight a little later without pushing the price over $640?

There is a 7:55 p.m. Sunday Delta nonstop arriving at 10:21 p.m. for $536 round trip. It remains under the airfare cap and raises the combined airfare-plus-extra-night estimate to $720. The earlier 6:18 p.m. option is $24 less and gives more recovery room if operations slip.
Narrow it to the earlier Sunday option and the Monday nonstop, both with the 7:32 Wednesday return. Don't book anything yet. I need the project manager to approve the extra hotel night.

The two finalists are: (1) Sunday, February 28, Delta nonstop at 6:18 p.m., arriving RDU at 8:44 p.m., with the Wednesday 7:32 p.m. nonstop return, $512 airfare plus an estimated $184 hotel night; and (2) Monday, March 1, Delta nonstop at 7:12 a.m., arriving at 10:36 a.m., with the same return, $618 airfare and no extra night. The Sunday plan costs about $78 more overall but removes the same-day arrival risk. Nothing has been booked; fares, hotel cost, and availability need rechecking after approval.
